title: GST-Perfringolysin O production for the localization and quantification of membrane cholesterol in human and mouse brain and liver
protocol: Obtain the DNA sequence of the PFO gene available at the NCBI database (NCBI: M36704).
Delete the leader sequence coding for 28 N-terminal amino acids.
Introduce the sequence 5′ GAA AAC CTG TAT TTT CAG GGC 3′ to encode the ENLYFQG motif recognized by Tobacco Etch Virus (TEV) protease.
Insert the modified construct into the pGEX-4T-1 vector using SmaI and EcoRI restriction sites.
Transform Escherichia coli (E. coli) BL21 (DE3) with the GST-PFO expressing pGEX 4T-1 vector.
Cryopreserve the transformed bacteria in Lysogeny Broth (LB) medium and 15% (v/v) glycerol and store at −80 °C.
Mix reagents to pre-grow the transformed bacteria in a 100 mL flask.
Incubate the flask at 220 rpm and 37°C overnight (12–24 h).
Take 1 ml of LB medium and ampicillin mix sample for spectrophotometer blank measurement.
Add pre-grown bacteria to a 1 L flask with additional reagents.
Measure absorbance of sample after adding pre-grown bacteria as "St0".
Incubate the flask at 220 rpm and 37°C.
Set up the spectrophotometer at 600 nm.
Adjust the spectrophotometer to rest the blank and read the “St0” sample.
Take aliquots approximately every 30 minutes.
Measure the absorbance of the samples until values reach 0.6 OD.
Add 0.5 mM of IPTG to induce GST-PFO production.
Incubate the flask for 20 hours at 220 rpm and 18°C.
Centrifuge the culture in four 50 mL falcons at 1600 g over 15 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Keep the pellets at −80°C.
Freeze the pellets at −80°C for a minimum of 30 minutes to help mechanical lysis.
Add 5 mL of “Lysis Solution” to each frozen pellet.
Mix with a pasteur pipette without adding oxygen to the sample on ice until solid traces of the pellet disappear from the liquid part.
Mix the four pellets in a 50 mL falcon.
Incubate the mixture for 30 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C) on a rotatory shaker at 30 rpm.
Centrifuge the lysate at 9000 g for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Collect and label the supernatant as “Total Protein Solution”.
Proceed with purification.
Use all reagents previously cooled and filtered with a 0.2 μm filter.
Perform GST-PFO purification by column affinity chromatography using prepacked Sepharose™ GST kit disposable columns and Glutathione Sepharose™ 4B medium.
For every 200 mL of initial induced culture, use 200 μL of the resin.
Equilibrate the column by adding 1 mL of “Binding buffer” and following the manufacturer's instructions.
Centrifuge the column at 500 g at 4°C for 5 min.
Discard supernatant by careful pipetting.
Repeat equilibration process two more times to ensure complete column equilibration.
Pipette 200 μL of resin into an eppendorf tube.
Add the “Total Protein Solution” sample to the resin and incubate at 4°C in a rotatory shaker at 30 rpm for 3 h.
Mount the elution column following the manufacturer's instructions and prepare your work area for gravity flow technique.
Add the “Total Protein Solution” sample to the column and collect the flow-through, labeling it as “Non-Bound”.
Wash the column with 3 mL of “Binding buffer” and collect the flow through, labeling it as “Wash” and its respective numeration.
Repeat washing process two more times.
Elute with 500 μL of Elution buffer.
Incubate the eluted sample for 10 minutes.
Allow the buffer to flow out.
Repeat the elution process two more times.
Label each elution sample and its corresponding number.
Take aliquots of 15 μL from each elution sample for SDS-PAGE gels.
Store all elution samples at -20°C until use.
Run an SDS-PAGE to analyze the collected samples from the purification step and decide which elution fractions dialyze together.
Select the eluted fractions with the purest and highest amounts of GST-PFO, pool them together in the same Amicon Ultra 15 mL centrifugal filters.
Dialyze the pooled fractions slowly with a “Dialysis Buffer”.
Centrifuge the Amicon Ultra 15 mL centrifugal filters at 5000 g for 10 min.
Calculate the concentration of glutathione per Amicon Ultra 15 mL centrifugal filter once eluted in the “Dialysis Buffer” using the recycling method based on Tietze (1969).
Repeat elutions until the concentration of glutathione in protein samples is 0.01 mM or less.
Aliquot the concentrated protein with low glutathione concentration and store 10 μL apart for Nanodrop quantification.
Add 20% (v/v) sucrose to the protein sample to prevent crystal formation.
Quantify protein concentration with 1 μL of the stored solution.
Calculate the corrected GST-PFO protein concentration using the formula: (GST-PFO protein concentration ÷ GST-PFO extinction coefficient) ∗ Extinction coefficient.
Adjust the concentration obtained by the formula to the volume of sucrose added per sample.
Aliquot the protein in adequate volumes for your assays.
Label each sample with its corresponding concentration.
Store samples at −80°C.
Immerse the tissue sample in “Fixation Solution” for 48 hours for human samples.
Wash the sample with “Cryoprotectant solution” to remove residual PFA traces.
Transfer the samples to “Cryoprotectant solution” containing 15% (w/v) sucrose until the samples sink, approximately 3 days.
Transfer the samples to “Cryoprotectant solution” containing 30% (w/v) sucrose until the samples sink, approximately 3 days.
Transfer the sample to a histology cassette and rinse it with M-1 Embedding Matrix.
Freeze the sample in dry ice.
Wrap the blocks in aluminum foil and label them.
Keep the histology cassettes at −80°C until sectioning.
Immerse the tissue sample in “Fixation Solution” for 24 hours.
Wash the sample with “Cryoprotectant solution” to remove residual PFA traces.
Adjust the camera of the cryostat to −19°C.
Adjust the sample holder head to −22°C.
Set the thickness of the slide to 30 μm.
Cut tissue sections from human and mouse brains.
Place cut sections on the slide.
Label the slide.
Store slides at −80°C.
Incubate samples in an orbital shaker at 10 rpm and 4°C.
Surround cut sections with a water-repellent pen.
Wash cut sections with PBS, three times for 5 minutes each to remove traces of PFA.
Apply NH4Cl-PBS (50 mM) over the cut sections.
Incubate the sections with NH4Cl-PBS for 40 minutes to quench fluorescence from PFA.
Wash with Triton X-100 1% over 30 minutes.
Block non-specific binding sites with 10% goat serum containing Triton X-100 1% for 2 hours and 30 minutes.
Apply GST-PFO at a concentration of 30 μg/mL for human tissue sections and 20 μg/mL for mouse tissue sections, diluted in “Immunofluorescence Solution”.
Incubate the treated sections with GST-PFO for 3 hours.
Wash cut sections with PBS for 10 minutes.
Incubate cut sections with primary antibodies diluted in “Immunofluorescence Solution” overnight at 4°C.
Wash cut sections with PBS for 10 minutes.
Apply secondary antibodies diluted 1:200 in “Immunofluorescence Solution” for 4 hours.
Add Sudan black 0.1% in 70% ethanol for 10 minutes to reduce autofluorescence.
Wash carefully with PBS until the sample is free from precipitates.
Remove excess liquid from the sample carefully using a paper towel.
Coverslip the samples with 8 μL of mounting media.
Let the mounted samples dry, avoiding air bubbles while mounting.
Visualize the mounted samples in a confocal microscope.
Store samples in darkness to avoid photobleaching.
Pause point: the mounted samples can be visualized up to 2 days after mounting if kept at 4°C.
